questions.q: Mr. Bello decided to buy a fire insurance policy for his neighbor's house. In the event of a fire outbreak, the insurance company will refuse to pay him because the contract violates the principle of...
questions.explain: The principle of **Insurable Interest** dictates that an individual can only insure an item if they would suffer a direct financial loss from its destruction. Since Mr. Bello does not own his neighbor's house, he has no insurable interest and cannot legally insure it.

questions.q: The fundamental insurance principle of *uberrimae fidei* strictly obligates the person taking out the insurance policy to...
options: surrender their damaged property to the insurance company after a claim.
disclose all material facts concerning the risk they wish to insure.
pay the insurance premium in equal monthly installments.
ensure they do not profit from a claim they make.
questions.explain: *Uberrimae Fidei* translates to **Utmost Good Faith**. It legally binds both the insurer and the insured to be completely honest and disclose every material fact related to the risk. Failure to disclose relevant information (like a pre-existing medical condition in life assurance) makes the policy voidable.

questions.q: Which of the following motor insurance policies is the legally mandated minimum for any vehicle owner driving on public roads in Nigeria?
questions.explain: **Third-Party Motor Insurance** is compulsory under the law for all vehicle owners. It covers injuries, death, or property damage caused to other people (the third party) by the insured vehicle, but does not cover the insured person's own vehicle.
